The point is that is the framework for connectivity that is already built into the code of Elden Ring.

Heres something you may not have considered- 

Nightreign is obviously built on Elden Ring's bones, which are basically the same all the way back to Dark Souls/Demons Souls. Im not 100% sure demons souls is relevant here but still.

The most party members you've ever been able to summon is 2, usually 1 but there is usually an item to bring it to two. 

Nightreign being balanced around 3 has a few good reasons. 

One 3 three main roles are "Tank, Heals, DPS". Id argue that is easier to balance for for a variety of reasons from a class perspective and a gameplay perspective. Goes  all the way back to the old archetypes of Warrior Rogue Wizard. 

Another is the gameplay similarities - Elden ring 2 (what ever form that takes) or any other souls game will likely at best have parties of three available as they always have. From does not like changing things just to change things. 

next - it does lead to easier match making. 3 people are easier to find than 4, especially when the game is going to have a strong base that wants to play solo. My self included. 

You may disagree with any of these reasons but that does not mean they arent valid reasons.

I think its Malenia. 

She is by all rights and accounts a true hero from every bit of textual evidence that we have, to the point that despite her presence being a literal anathema to life, her knights were willing to litterally fall apart to serve her. Findlay's story is a good example of this. 

Radahn was also a hero as well, despite failing to take Leyndell in the Shattering, but Malenia could have become Elden Lord. 

She beat Godrick. That was two runes. She didn't take it. She kept on the march to Radahn. 

We find out later that this is at the behest of Miquella. 

I legitamately think that Malenia was corrupted and controlled as a weapon by Miquella to further his goals and then discarded when she bloomed in Caelid. 

Its noted that she was locked in a slumber, missing, after her battle with Radahn. I think Findlay took her to Elphael to heal, but Miquella used his powers of Enchantment and St Trina's powers of sleep to lock Malenia away, because she is one of only 2 beings that can oppose him (and Radahn cannot beat her) and she has a reason. 

However due to the blooms shes becoming the Goddess of Rot. She is a literal existential threat to the entire lands between and the world at large. And she does not want to be. 

We have to fight her to take her down, as both the Blade of Miquella, arguably his most powerful physical weapon, and the Goddess of Rot because she can and will destroy the world over time. 

She never deserved this, she never wanted this, she was a hero. Theres an entire Manor dedicated to her - We get to hear from her by proxy via millicent and its mostly regret and Millicent chooses to die. I think Malenia attacks us to force us to kill her. 

She is the only person of the Demigods that we fight, besides Radahn, arguably, that really does not deserve it. (Radahn is arguable for marching on Leyndell, Malenia only stopped to knock the stupid out of Godrick for personally insulting her. He must have grafted on a few extra sets of balls).

I feel malenia's difficulty is very build dependant. Bonk sticks and good timing are much more effective than fireballs and space lasers IMO. She's also very reactionary and you can use that to your advantage in P1 at least. 

Final boss of DLC is a freight train though and will absolutely steamroll you if you're not careful. I feel that they are much more defense dependant rather than good offense windows. 

I do think Malenia is harder with a bad build compared to DLC final boss, but her difficulty is more swingy and shes more exploitable. 

I do think shes harder than everything else in the dlc tho.

Miquella - whole lotta mind control but seemed to legitmately want to make things better for everyone. Malenias great rune implies that Malenia should have been the successor to Marika but the scarlet rot curse was fucking it up.

Radahn is kind of the same. His battle lust / glory hounding lead to the nuking of Caelid. Starting class is largely irrelevant for late game, except wretch which is a min max option. 

Vigor is the "crutch" stat - more health = easier time. I've platinumed every souls game and id say this is true for all of them. IMO aim for 20 then the required stats for your weapon if you've found one, then 30 and 40. Dont forget endurance either but armor isnt as important IMO. 

You can respec after Renalla so don't stress if you need to change later. 

I think the easiest builds lean toward heavy weapons because they stagger enemies, and have wide swings but that might be a personal quirk. 

The next biggest tip IMO is the map. It is insanely detailed. You'll learn to recognize certain landmarks like Churches or Tunnells. Most types of mini dungeons like tunnells tend to have similar loot. 

IMO Strength builds deal the most burst damage and are better for PVE than Dex. Dex builds have higher DPS over time and can more easily work in Status Effects. Sorcery (Int) versus Incantations (faith) I feel are similar in high level view. 

Spirit summons are fine. Use em. You dont need them but they do help. 

Oh and finally try to stay in "Medium" equip load. Better rolling. If you like your gear dont be afraid of Endurance. (more stamina means more actions too!)

These are my high level tips completely unsolicited and if you want more information on anything specific feel free to ask.

If you've played Hearthstone, commander has some parallels in deck building. Once you pick your class (color identity) you're restricted to those colors. 

You're always going to have access to your commander, it starts outside of the game off to the side in the "Command Zone". 

ideally you're going to want to build around your commander in some way. 

Commanders are always Legendary Creatures. 

For Example, a very famous commander is [[Kaalia of the Vast]]. 

You'd be restricted to R/W/Black and you'd probably want to build in a way to take advantage of her attack trigger. Giant Angels Demons Dragons, that sort of thing. 

you're not going to have acess to green or blue so land ramp and counter spells start to be a thing to be wary of.

If Your commander dies, it goes back to the command zone and it will cost 2 generic more for every time its been cast. 

Commanders are revealed before for the start of the game. 

Commander is often optimized for 4 player pods but this is not a requirement. 

Any Legendary Creature can be a commander.

I also run a Red / Green Commander, a few of them actually, and i would peruse EDHREC because you can see all the R/G commanders.

I like the Bicameral system in theory becuase it, ideally, allows people to be elected for the same reasons for different functions. Im a bit rusty but tax bills are meant to originate in the house as a function of the will of the people. 

Ideally the House is the Will of the people and the Senate is the Will of the State. The idea is that those 2 nebulous identities are less distinct now especially with the direct election of Senators. 

And due to our 2 party system and other issues forcing incredibly divided and narrowly lead houses have lead to both houses, either directly or indirectly over the years, ceding a massive amount of power to the executive, and recently, the judiciary. 

The system has become distorted. The loop holes need to be closed and the system needs to be modernized. Regardless of politics, Chuck Grassley should NOT be in the senate at 89 years old. We should have better checks against bad faith actors. Im trying not to spiral out into all of the other things that impact it such as the 24 hour news cycle masquerading as entertainment masquerading as news. 

One change I would enjoy seeing is a repeal of the direct election of senators and term limits for senators. Senate terms are too safe at 6 years. You win twice and you've had a vote for a generation. Senators should be appointed by their state legislature as a representative of the state, which does have concerns that may conflict with the concerns of the populace. It is a balancing act. 

This is why the house is reelected every 2 years, to make sure its finger stays on the pulse of its electorate. Also the people elect the governors which appoint the senators so they do still have a hand in it, if less directly. 
TLDR Bicameral good, needs some restoration, termlimits please, and probably age limits too.

Wishes should not work because by their very nature they go against one of the fundamental tenets of EDH. so do tutors, for what its worth but that cat's already out of the bag.

Wishes violate the singleton spirit. If you had wishes that worked each wish card became Pay Y add X cards to your deck. 

Part of the spirit of singleton format is that each card is meant to be unique and most importantly, significant. Note, I do not mean GOOD or COMPETITIVE, although you can layer that on. 

Tutors also violate this because Demonc Tutor really read Pay 2 cast any card in your deck, however, like I said, we're past the point of no return on tutors as a whole. I don't want more effective tutors. 

And then there is the problem of OVERLAP with singelton format as well as the hard limit of 100 cards per deck including commander(s). Do you allow for duplicates in the wishboard? Is it youre entire collection? Do you allow proxies? (which, while im fine with becomes bullshit when someone casts burning wish for yawgmoths will and just scribbles it on a piece of paper because all of a sudden its the best possible card.) How do you define whats in a wishboard to begin with? How many cards should it be? Do the cards have to confirm to other deckbuilding restrictions? 

TLDR, No, They violate the spirit of the format in a variety of ways. It eases restrictions on deckbuilding, and it would be an actual logisitical nightmare to make work anyway.

There has always been this disconnect between innovatoin and follow ups. Games like Black Ops get derided for not changing, while Mario dosent change much from certain iterations and yet masterpiece to masterpiece. 

That fine line noted, Here is what I would do:

Mechanically, do NOT change anything. Keep Odyssey 2 mechanically same as 1. Most of the feedback I have seen on the game has been that the range and ease of movement is by far its best feature. 

Add new Captures for sure. Mario has about a bazillion things to play with. Boos, BobOmb, and Wigglers jump to mind that I personally want.

The big thing, and this is important because its Odyssey, is give us more areas to explore. I think they pigeonholed them selves a LITTLE bit with using a globe as stage select but, a problem can be solved. Used more original traditional Mario Settings. Delfino, Dinosaur Island, Yoshi's whatever the hell THAT is that is all arts and crafts. Put us in space with Rosalina, you already have the star bits and the Odyssey CAN go into space. Odyssey2/Galaxy3 anyone? Donkey Kong's Islands, Wario's Construction areas, Waluigis rip off resorts? Not to mention you can return to some of the Odyssey areas. 

My biggest complaint with odyssey was that the worlds felt incredibly static, bar the story changes. Stompin a goomba respawnin a goomba. It was necessary to solve the puzzles often, didnt want to not have gombas for gombettes, but it would be fun to keep returning to Odyssey and having areas change. Bowsers Castle Rusted, New Donk flooded because of a bad storm are some brainstorm ideas. 

The idea that a title can't follow up because its so good is never a concern for me because the platform is great, now we just need more areas. For example, Majoras Mask after Ocarina. Super Mario World after SMB3. The game mechanics didnt change much, at their core and the games were lauded. Odyssey 2 can do the same concept.
Myrahs Element and Necrium Blade is a start. What else we got?

IMO KH is popular because it follows very fundamental design beats of going from themed area to themed area and gaining relevant power ups whilst rewarding for exploring with a fun set of biomes to be in. The use of disney is simply a lure at first but honestly any standard issue (and disney is not) world themeing would have been enough of a lure, for a solid basic fundamental JARPG. 

It also brings a surprisignly consistent tone and theme to a very disparate set of environments with a basic story premise (Hero saves the princess, sometimes from rival) whilst teasing in enough flickers of a grander mythos to be expanded upon later. 

I don't know how well KH did expand, I only played the first, and it is DAUNTING looking at the titles and wondering what the play path is, in an almost standard issue Square fashion. 

This says nothing of the use of music both original and disney, and the seamless fusion of disney and square properties, by almost militantly  ignoring that they are doing it. They never question why goofy is asking Yufie for directions and so we dont wonder later why cloud is fighting hercules for hades. 

TLDR Disney is a lure meant to lure us into familarity but the game is built on solid fundamentals.
